Iut/Tripod/TwoAdic.lean:470. Uncompiled independent draft. -/
import Definitions.Def_TripodLegendreHeightComparisonInputs
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

set_option autoImplicit false
open NumberField

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod

noncomputable def infHeight {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T] (y : T) : ℝ :=
  ∑ w : InfinitePlace T, (w.mult : ℝ) * Real.posLog (w y)

theorem logHeight₁_eq_infHeight_add_finHeight {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T]
    (y : T) : Height.logHeight₁ y = infHeight y + finHeight y :=
  logHeight₁_eq y

theorem infHeight_nonneg {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T] (y : T) :
    0 ≤ infHeight y :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _) Real.posLog_nonneg

theorem finHeight_le_logHeight₁ {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T] (y : T) :
    finHeight y ≤ Height.logHeight₁ y := by
  rw [logHeight₁_eq_infHeight_add_finHeight]
  linarith [infHeight_nonneg y]

@[simp] theorem finHeight_zero {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T] :
    finHeight (0 : T) = 0 := by simp [finHeight]

theorem infHeight_le_of_forall {T : Type*} [Field T] [NumberField T] {y : T} {c : ℝ}
    (h : ∀ w : InfinitePlace T, Real.posLog (w y) ≤ c) :
    infHeight y ≤ c * Module.finrank ℚ T := by
  unfold infHeight
  calc ∑ w : InfinitePlace T, (w.mult : ℝ) * Real.posLog (w y)
      ≤ ∑ w : InfinitePlace T, (w.mult : ℝ) * c :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun w _ => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h w) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
    _ = c * Module.finrank ℚ T := by
        rw [← Finset.sum_mul, ← Nat.cast_sum, InfinitePlace.sum_mult_eq, mul_comm]

theorem posLog_le_abs_log (t : ℝ) : Real.posLog t ≤ |Real.log t| := by
  rw [Real.posLog_apply]
  exact max_le (abs_nonneg _) (le_abs_self _)

theorem posLog_inv_le_abs_log (t : ℝ) : Real.posLog t⁻¹ ≤ |Real.log t| := by
  rw [Real.posLog_apply, Real.log_inv]
  exact max_le (abs_nonneg _) (neg_le_abs _)

theorem CompactlyBounded.c_nonneg {K : CompactlyBounded} {x : Pt}
    (hx : x ∈ K.set) : 0 ≤ K.c := by
  obtain ⟨w⟩ : Nonempty (InfinitePlace (fieldOf x.1)) := inferInstance
  exact (abs_nonneg _).trans (hx.2 w).1

theorem gen_ne_one (x : Pt) : gen x.1 ≠ 1 :=
  sub_ne_zero.mp (gen_sub_one_ne_zero x.2.2)

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod

Original-source quotations for the Legendre height comparison. All quoted English below is from the original PDFs, checked against rendered pages. Mathematical notation is transcribed into KaTeX. Printed and one-based PDF page numbers coincide.

**Source iut4.** Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations*. [Official PDF](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Inter-universal%20Teichmuller%20Theory%20IV.pdf). SHA-256: `5bf4b1e0a8c2686562a6859e5009d301335044cfb5efec5d3a9edf764e4af87f`. The official download matches the repository PDF byte for byte.

**Source genell.** Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position*. [Official PDF](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Arithmetic%20Elliptic%20Curves%20in%20General%20Position.pdf). SHA-256: `b9dc115af61dca7fe434332ebafddf6a376a9e2926dad4e1ea2dcc0d2441f768`. The official download matches the repository PDF byte for byte.

**Corollary 2.2, setup and hypotheses through “Then:” — iut4, p.41.**

Corollary 2.2. (Construction of Suitable Initial $\Theta$-Data) Suppose that $X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is the projective line over $\mathbb{Q}$, and that $D\subseteq X$ is the divisor consisting of the three points “$0$”, “$1$”, and “$\infty$”. We shall regard $X$ as the “$\lambda$-line” — i.e., we shall regard the standard coordinate on $X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ as the “$\lambda$” in the Legendre form “$y^2=x(x-1)(x-\lambda)$” of the Weierstrass equation defining an elliptic curve — and hence as being equipped with a natural classifying morphism $U_X\to(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}$ [cf. the discussion preceding Proposition 1.8]. Let

$$
\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})
$$

be a compactly bounded subset [i.e., regarded as a subset of $X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ — cf. Remark 2.3.1, (vi), below; [GenEll], Example 1.3, (ii)] whose support contains the nonarchimedean prime “$2$”. Suppose further that $\mathcal{K}_V$ satisfies the following condition:

$(\ast_{j\text{-inv}})$ If $v\in\mathbb{V}(\mathbb{Q})$ denotes the nonarchimedean prime “$2$”, then the image of the subset $\mathcal{K}_v\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v)$ associated to $\mathcal{K}_V$ [cf. the notational conventions of [GenEll], Example 1.3, (ii)] via the $j$-invariant $U_X\to(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\mathbb{A}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is a bounded subset of $\mathbb{A}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v)=\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v$, i.e., is contained in a subset of the form $2^{N_{j\text{-inv}}}\cdot\mathcal{O}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v}\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v$, where $N_{j\text{-inv}}\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathcal{O}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v}\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_v$ denotes the ring of integers.

Then:

**Corollary 2.2(i), complete statement — iut4, p.41.**

(i) Write “$\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})$” (respectively, “$\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\nmid 2}_{(-)})$”) for the $\mathbb{R}$-valued function on $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, hence also on $U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$, obtained by forming the normalized degree “$\underline{\deg}(-)$” of the effective arithmetic divisor determined by the q-parameters of an elliptic curve over a number field at arbitrary nonarchimedean primes (respectively, at the nonarchimedean primes that do not divide $2$) [cf. the invariant “$\log(\mathfrak{q})$” associated, in the statement of Theorem 1.10, to the elliptic curve $E_F$]. Also, we shall write $\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}$ for the [normalized] height function on $U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ — a function which is well-defined up to a “bounded discrepancy” [cf. the discussion preceding [GenEll], Proposition 3.4] — determined by the pull-back to $X$ of the divisor at infinity of the natural compactification $(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Then we have an equality of “bounded discrepancy classes” [cf. [GenEll], Definition 1.2, (ii), as well as Remark 2.3.1, (ii), below]

$$
\frac{1}{6}\cdot\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\nmid 2}_{(-)})\approx\frac{1}{6}\cdot\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})\approx\frac{1}{6}\cdot\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}\approx\mathrm{ht}_{\omega_X(D)}
$$

of functions on $\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$.

**Proof of Corollary 2.2(i), complete proof — iut4, p.43.**

Proof. First, we consider assertion (i). We begin by observing that, in light of the condition $(\ast_{j\text{-inv}})$ that was imposed on $\mathcal{K}_V$, it follows immediately from the various definitions involved that

$$
\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\nmid 2}_{(-)})\approx\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})
$$

— where we observe that the function “$\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})$” may be identified with the function “$\underline{\deg}_{\infty}$” of the discussion preceding [GenEll], Proposition 3.4 — on $\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$. In a similar vein, since the support of $\mathcal{K}_V$ contains the unique archimedean prime of $\mathbb{Q}$, it follows immediately from the various definitions involved [cf. also Remark 2.3.1, (vi), below] that

$$
\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})\approx\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}
$$

on $\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ [cf. the argument of the final paragraph of the proof of [GenEll], Lemma 3.7]. Thus, we conclude that $\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\nmid 2}_{(-)})\approx\log(\mathfrak{q}^{\forall}_{(-)})\approx\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}$ on $\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$. Finally, since [as is well-known] the pull-back to $X$ of the divisor at infinity of the natural compactification $(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}})_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is of degree $6$, while the line bundle $\omega_X(D)$ is of degree $1$, the equality of BD-classes $\frac{1}{6}\cdot\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}\approx\mathrm{ht}_{\omega_X(D)}$ on $\mathcal{K}_V\subseteq U_X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ follows immediately from [GenEll], Proposition 1.4, (i), (iii). This completes the proof of assertion (i).

**Proposition 3.4, complete statement — genell, p.17.**

Proposition 3.4. (Faltings Heights and the Divisor at Infinity) For any $\epsilon\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, we have

$$
\underline{\deg}_{\infty}\lesssim\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}\lesssim12(1+\epsilon)\cdot\mathrm{ht}^{\mathrm{Falt}}\lesssim(1+\epsilon)\cdot\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}
$$

on $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$. In particular, if $C\in\mathbb{R}$, then the set of points $[E]\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})^{\leq d}$ such that $\mathrm{ht}^{\mathrm{Falt}}([E])\leq C$ is finite.

**Proof of Lemma 3.7, paragraph beginning “Now suppose that condition (b)”, first two sentences — genell, p.19.**

Now suppose that condition (b) is satisfied. Recall that by definition $\mathrm{ht}_{\infty}([E_L])$ may be computed as the sum of $\underline{\deg}_{\infty}([E_L])$ and an archimedean term which, in the present situation, is bounded, since $[E_L]\in\mathcal{K}_V$.

**Fidelity limits and relation to the Lean unit.**

- The exact source match for legendreHeight is the parent bounded-discrepancy comparison in IUT IV Corollary 2.2(i), with its proof identifying log(q^forall) with normalized degree at infinity and using the degrees 6 and 1. The chosen normalized Weil-height representative htCan is an implementation choice.

- The constants log(2)/3 and c*|V|+c+log(2)/3 in legendreHeight are supplied by the Lean proof. They are not printed in the cited original passages.

- The three-term archimedean estimate logHeight_1(y)<=finHeight(y)+c*d for y=lambda,lambda^(-1),(lambda-1)^(-1) has only a parent-level source in the bounded archimedean term described in [GenEll] Lemma 3.7 and the compact-bounded comparison in IUT IV. No exact three-term estimate or constant c*d was found in these passages.

- The finite-part inequalities in finHeight_legendreJ_le and finHeight_legendreJ_ge, including factors 2 and 6*c*|V|*d, are implementation-specific elementary estimates under the parent comparison. They must not be presented as verbatim statements of Corollary 2.2(i) or Proposition 3.4.

- The elementary auxiliary lemma j(lambda)=0 implies lambda^6=1 is not stated in the cited original source passages. No direct original quotation for that lemma was located in the two PDFs. Cite the parent height-comparison obligation only, and label this step an auxiliary derivation.

- [GenEll] Proposition 3.4 is a Faltings-height comparison, not the direct statement of the Legendre finite-part estimates. The archimedean boundedness paragraph actually referenced by the IUT IV proof is [GenEll] Lemma 3.7, p.19.

- The quotations retain the paper hypotheses, including support containing 2 and the condition (*j-inv). These source quotations do not certify that each Lean structure has already been shown to imply every paper hypothesis.

**Typesetting normalization.**

- Original English words, sentence order, punctuation, bracketed comments, and quoted labels are retained; line wrapping and discretionary line-end hyphens are removed, and ligatures are expanded.

- Mathematical typesetting is transcribed into KaTeX. Fraktur q uses \mathfrak{q}; calligraphic moduli and bounding sets use \mathcal; normalized degree preserves the original underline as \underline{\deg}; Faltings height preserves the original superscript as \mathrm{ht}^{\mathrm{Falt}}.

- Italic/bold prose, equation spacing and display alignment are normalized; the relation printed as a less-than sign with a wavy underline is rendered with \lesssim.

- The q-parameter with superscript for primes not dividing 2 is rendered as \mathfrak{q}^{\nmid 2}; the all-primes symbol is rendered as \forall, as verified visually.

- No explicit Lean constants or local inequalities have been inserted into any quotation.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.infHeight`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. Define hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logHeight₁_eq_infHeight_add_finHeight`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. For every y, hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y).

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.infHeight_nonneg`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. For every y, 0 ≤ hinf,F(y).

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.finHeight_le_logHeight₁`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. For every y, hfin,F(y) ≤ hrel,F(y).

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.finHeight_zero`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. The finite relative logarithmic height of 0 is hfin,F(0) = 0.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.infHeight_le_of_forall`

For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. For any real c, if log⁺|y|w ≤ c at EVERY infinite place w of F, then hinf,F(y) ≤ c[F:Q]. No sign assumption on c is imposed.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.posLog_le_abs_log`

For every real t, max(0,log t) ≤ |log t|, using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0 (and log t = log|t| for t < 0).

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.posLog_inv_le_abs_log`

For every real t, max(0,log(t⁻¹)) ≤ |log t|. Real inversion is total with 0⁻¹ = 0, and log 0 = 0; no positivity or nonzero hypothesis is required.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded.c_nonneg`

Let λ be an element of the fixed algebraic closure Q̄ of Q with λ ≠ 0,1, let x denote this point, and let Fλ = Q(λ) be the full simple subfield of Q̄ generated by λ. All occurrences of λ inside height and place expressions mean the canonical generator in Fλ. Put dλ = [Fλ:Q] = degree of the minimal polynomial of λ. At a finite place v corresponding to a nonzero prime ideal 𝔭 of the ring of integers of Fλ, use |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At an infinite place w use the usual real absolute value or complex modulus with multiplicity mw = 1 or 2, respectively. Write log⁺ t = max(0, log t), with the total real logarithm log 0 = 0. Define hfin,F(y) = Σ over ALL finite places v of F of log⁺|y|v, hinf,F(y) = Σ over infinite places w of F of mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). These are relative heights, with no division by [F:Q]. The absolute logarithmic point height is hcan(x) = hrel,Fλ(λ)/dλ. Set Jλ = 256(λ²−λ+1)³/[λ²(λ−1)²] and a(x) = hfin,Fλ(Jλ)/dλ. In particular, a(x) uses Fλ, which need not be Q(Jλ). All logarithms are natural. A bounded-set datum K consists of a finite set V of rational prime numbers with 2 ∈ V and a real number c, with no separate axiom c ≥ 0. A point belongs to K precisely when |log|λ|v| ≤ c and |log|λ−1|v| ≤ c for every finite place v of Fλ whose residue characteristic belongs to V, and the same two bounds hold for EVERY infinite place of Fλ. Finite places with residue characteristic outside V are not constrained by membership in K; they are still included in every finite-height sum. Write #V for the number of distinct rational primes in V. Nonemptiness of K implies c ≥ 0. For every K and every point x ∈ K, c ≥ 0.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.gen_ne_one`

Let λ be an element of the fixed algebraic closure Q̄ of Q with λ ≠ 0,1, let x denote this point, and let Fλ = Q(λ) be the full simple subfield of Q̄ generated by λ. All occurrences of λ inside height and place expressions mean the canonical generator in Fλ. Put dλ = [Fλ:Q] = degree of the minimal polynomial of λ. At a finite place v corresponding to a nonzero prime ideal 𝔭 of the ring of integers of Fλ, use |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At an infinite place w use the usual real absolute value or complex modulus with multiplicity mw = 1 or 2, respectively. Write log⁺ t = max(0, log t), with the total real logarithm log 0 = 0. Define hfin,F(y) = Σ over ALL finite places v of F of log⁺|y|v, hinf,F(y) = Σ over infinite places w of F of mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). These are relative heights, with no division by [F:Q]. The absolute logarithmic point height is hcan(x) = hrel,Fλ(λ)/dλ. Set Jλ = 256(λ²−λ+1)³/[λ²(λ−1)²] and a(x) = hfin,Fλ(Jλ)/dλ. In particular, a(x) uses Fλ, which need not be Q(Jλ). All logarithms are natural. For every such point x, its generator λ in Fλ is not 1.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.infHeight`

对任意数域 F 及其中元素 y，有限位绝对值归一化为非零 y 时 |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))，且 |0|v = 0。无穷位使用实绝对值与复模，权重 mw 分别为 1 与 2。记 log⁺ t = max(0,log t)，全定义实对数规定 log 0 = 0。hfin,F(y) 为 F 的全部有限位上的 log⁺|y|v 之和，hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w，hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。这些和是未除以 [F:Q] 的相对对数高度；对应绝对对数高度为 hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]。 定义无穷位相对对数高度 hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logHeight₁_eq_infHeight_add_finHeight`

对任意数域 F 及其中元素 y，有限位绝对值归一化为非零 y 时 |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))，且 |0|v = 0。无穷位使用实绝对值与复模，权重 mw 分别为 1 与 2。记 log⁺ t = max(0,log t)，全定义实对数规定 log 0 = 0。hfin,F(y) 为 F 的全部有限位上的 log⁺|y|v 之和，hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w，hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。这些和是未除以 [F:Q] 的相对对数高度；对应绝对对数高度为 hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]。 对所有 y，有 hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.infHeight_nonneg`

对任意数域 F 及其中元素 y，有限位绝对值归一化为非零 y 时 |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))，且 |0|v = 0。无穷位使用实绝对值与复模，权重 mw 分别为 1 与 2。记 log⁺ t = max(0,log t)，全定义实对数规定 log 0 = 0。hfin,F(y) 为 F 的全部有限位上的 log⁺|y|v 之和，hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w，hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。这些和是未除以 [F:Q] 的相对对数高度；对应绝对对数高度为 hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]。 对所有 y，无穷位相对对数高度满足 0 ≤ hinf,F(y)。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.finHeight_le_logHeight₁`

对任意数域 F 及其中元素 y，有限位绝对值归一化为非零 y 时 |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))，且 |0|v = 0。无穷位使用实绝对值与复模，权重 mw 分别为 1 与 2。记 log⁺ t = max(0,log t)，全定义实对数规定 log 0 = 0。hfin,F(y) 为 F 的全部有限位上的 log⁺|y|v 之和，hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w，hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。这些和是未除以 [F:Q] 的相对对数高度；对应绝对对数高度为 hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]。 对所有 y，有限位相对对数高度满足 hfin,F(y) ≤ hrel,F(y)。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.finHeight_zero`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded.c_nonneg`

设 λ 是固定有理数域代数闭包 Q̄ 中不等于 0、1 的元素，x 表示该点，Fλ = Q(λ) 是由 λ 生成的完整单扩张子域。高度和地方表达式中的 λ 均指 Fλ 中的标准生成元。令 dλ = [Fλ:Q]，即 λ 的最小多项式次数。对 Fλ 整数环的非零素理想 𝔭 所对应的有限位 v，非零 y 的绝对值取为 |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))，且 |0|v = 0；无穷位 w 使用通常的实绝对值或复模，权重 mw 分别为 1 或 2。记 log⁺ t = max(0, log t)，其中全定义实对数规定 log 0 = 0。定义 hfin,F(y) 为 F 的全部有限位上的 log⁺|y|v 之和，hinf,F(y) 为全部无穷位上的 mw log⁺|y|w 之和，hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y)。这些是相对高度，尚未除以 [F:Q]。点的绝对对数高度为 hcan(x) = hrel,Fλ(λ)/dλ。令 Jλ = 256(λ²−λ+1)³/[λ²(λ−1)²]，a(x) = hfin,Fλ(Jλ)/dλ。特别地，a(x) 在完整点域 Fλ 中计算，Fλ 未必等于 Q(Jλ)。所有对数均为自然对数。 有界集合数据 K 由包含 2 的有限有理素数集 V 和实数 c 组成，结构中未另行假设 c ≥ 0。点属于 K 当且仅当：对 Fλ 中剩余特征属于 V 的每个有限位 v，均有 |log|λ|v| ≤ c 和 |log|λ−1|v| ≤ c；对 Fλ 的每个无穷位也同时满足这两个界。剩余特征不属于 V 的有限位不受集合成员条件限制，但仍全部计入有限高度之和。#V 表示 V 中不同有理素数的个数。K 非空可推出 c ≥ 0。 对每个 K 及其中任一点 x，都有 c ≥ 0。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded.c_nonneg`

λ を固定した Q の代数閉包 Q̄ の元で 0,1 と異なるものとし、x をその点とする。Fλ = Q(λ) は λ が生成する完全な単拡大部分体であり、高さと素点の式の λ は Fλ の標準生成元を表す。dλ = [Fλ:Q] は λ の最小多項式の次数である。Fλ の整数環の非零素イデアル 𝔭 に対応する有限素点 v では、非零 y に対して |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y))、また |0|v = 0 とする。無限素点 w では通常の実絶対値または複素絶対値を用い、重み mw はそれぞれ 1,2 とする。log⁺ t = max(0, log t) とし、全域で定義された実対数は log 0 = 0 とする。hfin,F(y) は F のすべての有限素点の log⁺|y|v の和、hinf,F(y) はすべての無限素点の mw log⁺|y|w の和、hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y) と定義する。これらは [F:Q] で割らない相対高さである。点の絶対対数高さは hcan(x) = hrel,Fλ(λ)/dλ である。Jλ = 256(λ²−λ+1)³/[λ²(λ−1)²] および a(x) = hfin,Fλ(Jλ)/dλ とする。特に a(x) は完全な点の体 Fλ で計算され、Fλ は Q(Jλ) と等しいとは限らない。対数はすべて自然対数である。 有界集合のデータ K は、2 を含む有理素数の有限集合 V と実数 c からなる。構造自体は c ≥ 0 を仮定しない。点が K に属する条件は、Fλ の剰余標数が V に属するすべての有限素点 v で |log|λ|v| ≤ c かつ |log|λ−1|v| ≤ c が成立し、Fλ のすべての無限素点でも同じ二つの不等式が成立することである。剰余標数が V に属さない有限素点にはこの所属条件からの制約はないが、有限高さの和にはすべて含める。#V は V に含まれる異なる有理素数の個数である。K が空でなければ c ≥ 0 が従う。 任意の K と x ∈ K に対し c ≥ 0 である。
